video.title: Is Year 3 The Prime Breakout Time In The NBA? [Breakout Fantasy Basketball Players]

summary: Josh Lloyd looks at third-year players as fantasy breakout candidates. Data from 2022-23 through 2025-26 shows big jumps from year two to year three in top 50 finishes. Lately, though, more of the big breakouts happen in year two, and late-round flyers on third-year players have rarely paid off. He reviews last season's third-year class (Wembanyama, the Thompson twins, Keyonte George, Brandon Miller), then turns to the current third-year class, which he calls a weak draft class that is often priced wrong. He thinks Donovan Clingan, Alex Sarr and Stephon Castle (in category leagues) are overdrafted. He is skeptical of Kyshawn George, Reed Sheppard, Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain. He likes Matas Buzelis, Zach Edey (if healthy) and Kel'el Ware as undervalued.

rules.text: In recent years the big breakouts have moved more to year two. Players who did not take a step in year two are the ones who tend to break out in year three.
rules.quote: over the last couple of years, we're getting more of the big improvements in year two

rules.text: Big jumps in year four are unlikely for players who have shown nothing in their first three years.

rules.text: Category-league breakouts are driven by efficiency at volume, a higher free throw attempt rate and a higher assist rate. Points leagues reflect these less.

rules.text: Third-year players drafted inside the top 50 have not busted badly. Third-year players drafted between 101 and 150 made the top 100 only 13% of the time.
rules.quote: Only 13% of those guys drafted late as third round players made it into the top 100.
